m.n: Eschatology: Death, Judgment, Purgatory, Heaven & Hell

co.n: Eschatology: Death, Judgment, Purgatory, Heaven & Hell Cohort

c.p: What is the Catholic doctrine of Purgatory?
c.a: a state of final purification for those who die in god's grace but require cleansing before entering heaven | final purification before entering heaven | purification of souls destined for heaven
c.h: All souls in Purgatory are assured of heaven; it is a purification of love aided by the prayers of the faithful on earth.
c.e: Purgatory is the final cleansing of the elect so as to achieve the holiness necessary to enter the joy of heaven; the Church commends suffrages, prayers, and the Mass on their behalf (CCC 1030–1032).
r: second chance for souls condemned hell
Purgatory is not a second chance for the damned; it is exclusively for those who died in friendship with God who need purification before beholding the Beatific Vision.
eternal resting place where souls remain forever
Purgatory is temporary; every soul purified in Purgatory ultimately enters eternal life in Heaven.

c.p: How does Catholic theology define Hell (eternal damnation)?
c.a: the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with god and the blessed | definitive self exclusion from god | eternal separation from god through unrepented mortal sin
c.h: It is the tragic outcome of human free will freely choosing to reject God's mercy and love until death.
c.e: Hell is the definitive state of self-chosen exclusion from communion with God, brought about by dying in mortal sin without repenting and refusing God's merciful love (CCC 1033–1037).
r: place god arbitrarily pushes innocent people into
God predestines no one to go to hell; a willful turning away from God (mortal sin) and persistence in it until the end is necessary for damnation.
